c2512a883f1d.name: AIM Investments
c2512a883f1d.text: Meta raises $35 billion for its AI ambitions. The offering includes $22.5B in Class A common stock and $12.5B in preferred stock, which converts into common shares in 2029.
c2512a883f1d.note: Breaks down the deal: $22.5B common plus $12.5B mandatory convertible preferred

c2512a883f1d.name: Stefan Schippers
c2512a883f1d.text: Meta plans $95bn stock offering to bankroll AI expansion… backed by chipmakers Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom, who will act as cornerstone investors
c2512a883f1d.note: Relays the FT report: $95B total program with NVDA, AMD and AVGO as cornerstones

c2512a883f1d.name: amitush
c2512a883f1d.text: $META just announced a dual capital raise: depositary shares representing Series A Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock, plus a simultaneous Class A common stock offering via forward sale agreements.
c2512a883f1d.note: ECM detail: the common piece is done via forward sales, which delays share issuance

c2512a883f1d.name: T$
c2512a883f1d.text: $META launched a $22.5B Class A share offering via forward sales plus mandatory convertible preferred shares. Stock fell as much as 2.3% premarket.

d7acdc244b1f.name: Elon Musk
d7acdc244b1f.text: Pretty much. As of the past few weeks, debt markets have almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn't have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers. SpaceX closed $40B of debt for GPUs, but we're investment grade and have Starlink & launch…
d7acdc244b1f.note: The source post: Musk says AI data center credit has dried up for pure-play neoclouds

d7acdc244b1f.name: Elon Musk
d7acdc244b1f.text: This is primarily callable debt for GPU purchases that will arrive in Q1 and Q2. Not a major factor this quarter.
d7acdc244b1f.note: Musk on the structure: callable debt tied to GPU deliveries in Q1-Q2

d7acdc244b1f.name: Elon Musk
d7acdc244b1f.text: SpaceX is not buying any neoclouds. Pointless.
d7acdc244b1f.note: Rules out SpaceX as a consolidator of distressed GPU clouds

d7acdc244b1f.name: Techmeme
d7acdc244b1f.text: Elon Musk says SpaceX closed $40B in GPU debt, debt markets have shut off credit for AI data center firms, and 200+ neoclouds face "death and consolidation"

d7acdc244b1f.name: Bingo
d7acdc244b1f.text: $CRWV Credit markets are drawing a hard line for AI data center operators. SpaceX locked $40B in GPU debt, but it's investment-grade, backed by Starlink + launch revenue. Lenders are shutting funding doors for pure GPU rental plays with no outside income.
d7acdc244b1f.note: Ties the comment to CoreWeave and other pure-play neoclouds

3fccf913600c.name: News Gurus
3fccf913600c.text: $TSLA $SPCX: two sell-side calls this morning point to the same Tesla–SpaceX merger thesis. Dan Ives puts the odds of a merger by 2027 at 80%–90%. He has Outperform on SpaceX with a $225 target and says a deal could value Tesla above $500 a share.
3fccf913600c.note: Sell-side read on deal odds and value

3fccf913600c.name: amir
3fccf913600c.text: Musk backs a SpaceX-Tesla merger, but he can't be in the room where it's decided. Both boards formed special committees. No terms agreed, no guarantee, yet he's the biggest individual shareholder of both. Can independent directors really say no to Musk?
3fccf913600c.note: The governance question: conflicted controller and special committees

3fccf913600c.name: Mike Ryan
3fccf913600c.text: In what could be the biggest merger ever, the buyer and the seller are effectively the same person. Both boards have formed special committees of independent directors to study it.
3fccf913600c.note: Frames the related-party problem in one line

3fccf913600c.name: Mike
3fccf913600c.text: Tesla shareholders with 17M+ shares signed a petition in 48 hours urging a Tesla-SpaceX merger. Musk says independent board committees are exploring it.
3fccf913600c.note: Retail shareholder pressure for a deal

00d70f725bbb.name: Nic
00d70f725bbb.text: BIG week ahead! $10 trillion in tech earnings. Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon. All expected to post strong revenue growth, but that's not what matters. The market wants to know one thing: how much are you burning on AI, and when does it show up in free cash flow?
00d70f725bbb.note: Most-engaged preview: capex vs free cash flow is the test

00d70f725bbb.name: Alex | The Profit Zone
00d70f725bbb.text: Alphabet $GOOG and Microsoft $MSFT report Wednesday after close, just hours after the Fed's rate decision, with Amazon $AMZN following Thursday.
00d70f725bbb.note: Timing: GOOGL and MSFT print hours after the Fed

00d70f725bbb.name: Julie
00d70f725bbb.text: Hyperscalers are guiding roughly $700–750B in 2026 capex (Amazon ~$220B, Alphabet $195–205B, Microsoft ~$175B, Meta $135–145B).
00d70f725bbb.note: Capex scoreboard going into the prints (user figures, verify)

00d70f725bbb.name: Patricio Mainardi
00d70f725bbb.text: The AI trade just met its real constraint: not demand, but the cost of funding it. The 10-year Treasury ending near 4.99%.
00d70f725bbb.note: Funding cost angle, which links to Meta's equity raise and Musk's credit comment
